newsitem.title: UK: Nthn Ireland Elec up after regulator report.
newsitem.headline: Nthn Ireland Elec up after regulator report.

text.p: Shares in Northern Ireland Electricity Plc rose in pre-market trade on Friday as the industry regulator announced details of its findings following a review by the Monopolies and Mergers Commission.
The company said it would hold an analyst briefing later today. The stock was marked 11p higher at 391p by 0725 GMT, though no volume was recorded.
Analysts noted that the MMC had recommended a smaller cut in transmission prices than sought by the regulator, and though the final outcome was as yet uncertain the news was positive for NIE shares.
"The position is very confused," said Nigel Hawkins, analyst at Yamaichi, "but NIE has got real change out of the MMC and that is good for the share price."
Issues like transmission and distribution prices for electricity companies are based on a complex analysis of the value of those companies' assets and the rate of depreciation of those assets.
Differing views on these issues determine how profitable the company will be and lie behind the different findings revealed today of the regulator, the MMC and the company.
Hawkins noted that the MMC had concluded a 25 percent price cut was warranted, compared with the 31 percent the regulator had sought and the 22 percent the company had offered.

The regulator said he was not minded fully to accept the MMC's conclusions to the extent determined by a proposed change to the company's depreciation policy for pre-flotation assets and had asked the company to produce the corporate plan on which the MMC's findings were based.
In the meantime, he said he was "minded" to allow the MMC proposals to stand for the next two years, followed by his proposals for the following three years of the price control period.
